payload.rationale:
Without specific data on the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season up to September 19, 2026, I must rely on climatological averages. The 1991-2020 NOAA average for an Atlantic hurricane season is 3.2 major hurricanes (Category 3 or higher). The baseline probability of experiencing 4 or more major hurricanes in a given season is historically around 40-45%, especially considering recent active seasons. 

Strongest reason my estimate could be too high: The 2026 season might be experiencing an El Niño pattern, which typically increases wind shear in the Atlantic and suppresses hurricane formation, leading to fewer than 3 major hurricanes. Furthermore, without knowing the current count as of September 19, the season could already be unusually quiet.

Strongest reason my estimate could be too low: If 2026 is a La Niña year or features exceptionally warm sea surface temperatures in the Main Development Region, the season could be hyperactive. Additionally, by mid-September, the peak of the season has occurred; if several major hurricanes have already formed, the true probability of exceeding 3 would be much higher than the baseline.
limitations: No real-time data on the number of major hurricanes that have already occurred by September 19, 2026.
No information on the ENSO state (El Niño/La Niña) or Atlantic sea surface temperatures for 2026.
Reliance on historical base rates which may not fully capture recent climate-driven trends.
